The core insight of 0701 is that distributional regression can incorporate a reject option by defining a decision boundary based on CRPS entropy. The optimal rule Γ*_λ(X) accepts predictions whose entropy does not exceed a threshold λ, otherwise rejecting them. This directly maps to the GSE publish-gate problem, where predictions with high uncertainty (high entropy) are withheld. The entropy threshold λ is chosen such that the overall rejection rate matches a desired ε, achieved via inverse empirical entropy CDF G_ent^{-1}(1-ε). The semi-supervised estimator uses labeled data to fit distributional models and unlabeled data to estimate the entropy distribution, ensuring that the rejection rate is controlled precisely. The theoretical guarantee E[|r(Γ̂_ε) - ε|] ≤ CN^{-1/2} ensures convergence of actual to target rejection rate. In GSI, this framework supports Bayesian inference by treating entropy as a measure of predictive uncertainty. In GSE, it enables state transitions between publish and withhold based on entropy thresholds, aligning with the need for risk-sensitive forecasting in sports intelligence.
